newsitem.title: USA: TCF Financial loan charge offs rise.
newsitem.headline: TCF Financial loan charge offs rise.

text.p: TCF Financial Corp said Wednesday its net loan charge offs rose to $4.5 million in the fourth quarter of 1996, from $1.3 million in the year-ago period.
But the increase is tied to a move by the $7.1 billion asset savings bank holding company to higher risk, higher yielding loans, TCF said.

"All of our banks continued to shift their product mix toward higher-yielding consumer loans and lower interest-cost retail deposit accounts, which significantly increased our net interest margin and fee income over last year," TCF chief executive William Cooper said in a news release.
Non-interest income was $39.8 million in the quarter, excluding a $1.8 million net gain from the sale of two Minnesota branches and related loans, TCF said.
That compares to $35.6 million a year ago, TCF said.
Earlier Wednesday, TCF reported net income of $27.4 million, or $0.79 a share before special charges, compared to $25.5 million, or $0.71 a share, a year ago.
